bibl.title: The echo chamber effect on social media

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: echo chambers on social media - whether they exist, and whether their existence is a property of online interaction or of a particular platform's design
span.quote: We can broadly define echo chambers as environments in which the opinion, political leaning, or belief of users about a topic gets reinforced due to repeated interactions with peers or sources having similar tendencies and attitudes.

span.label: whether the echo chamber effect survives a comparison across platforms with different interaction paradigms, measured the same way on each
span.quote: We introduce an operational definition of echo chambers to provide a common methodological ground to explore how different platforms influence their formation. In particular, we operationalize the two common elements that characterize echo chambers into observables that can be quantified and empirically measured, namely, 1) the inference of the user’s leaning for a specific topic (e.g., politics, vaccines) and 2) the structure of their social interactions on the platform.

span.label: an operational definition of echo chambers - individual leaning plus interaction structure, quantified independently - applied identically to Facebook, Twitter, Reddit and Gab over 100 million pieces of content
span.quote: We introduce an operational definition of echo chambers to provide a common methodological ground to explore how different platforms influence their formation. In particular, we operationalize the two common elements that characterize echo chambers into observables that can be quantified and empirically measured, namely, 1) the inference of the user’s leaning for a specific topic (e.g., politics, vaccines) and 2) the structure of their social interactions on the platform.

span.label: existence
span.quote: These results indicate that information diffusion is biased toward individuals who share a similar leaning in some social media, namely Twitter and Facebook. In contrast, in others—Reddit and Gab in our analysis—this effect is absent.

span.label: aggregation of users into homophilic clusters, and the bias it puts on which information reaches whom - present on some platforms and absent on others
span.quote: Furthermore, we find significant differences across platforms in terms of homophilic patterns in the network structure and biases in the information diffusion toward like-minded users. A clear-cut distinction emerges between social media having a feed algorithm tweakable by the users (e.g., Reddit) and social media that don’t provide such an option (e.g., Facebook and Twitter).

span.label: leaning inferred per user from endorsed or linked content, interaction networks reconstructed per platform, then homophily measured against neighbour leaning and diffusion bias measured by SIR dynamics over the network
span.term: leaning inferred per user from endorsed or linked content, interaction networks reconstructed per platform, then homophily measured against neighbour leaning and diffusion bias measured by SIR dynamics over the network
span.quote: Facebook and Reddit are particularly apt to a cross-comparison since they share the definition of individual leaning (computed by using the classification provided by mediabiasfactcheck.org; see Materials and Methods for further details) and the rationale in creating connections among users that is based on an interaction network.

span.label: when a user's neighbours share their leaning, a message released by that user reaches an audience with the same leaning; running an epidemic model over the interaction network turns that structural fact into a measurable dependence of the influence set's leaning on the seed's
span.quote: These results indicate that information diffusion is biased toward individuals who share a similar leaning in some social media, namely Twitter and Facebook. In contrast, in others—Reddit and Gab in our analysis—this effect is absent.

span.label: platforms that choose a user's content for them, and platforms where the user selects their own communities, produce different network topologies from the same human tendencies - so the effect divides along a design decision rather than along the population
span.quote: Furthermore, we find significant differences across platforms in terms of homophilic patterns in the network structure and biases in the information diffusion toward like-minded users. A clear-cut distinction emerges between social media having a feed algorithm tweakable by the users (e.g., Reddit) and social media that don’t provide such an option (e.g., Facebook and Twitter).

span.label: a measurement of contrast between leanings can only see a difference that exists inside the sample; if a platform's whole population shares one leaning, the measurement returns the same null it would return if there were no echo chamber at all
span.quote: Such a latter configuration may depend upon two factors: 1) Gab and Reddit are not bursting the echo chamber effects, or 2) we are observing the dynamic inside a single echo chamber.

span.label: the null result on Reddit and Gab is explicitly ambiguous - either those platforms are not producing echo chambers, or the observation is being made inside a single one, and the data cannot separate the two
span.quote: Such a latter configuration may depend upon two factors: 1) Gab and Reddit are not bursting the echo chamber effects, or 2) we are observing the dynamic inside a single echo chamber.

span.label: every individual leaning in the study is derived from one external labelling of 2,190 news outlets, so the whole comparison inherits that organisation's judgements
span.quote: The labeling of news outlets is based on the information reported by Media Bias/Fact Check (MBFC) (https://mediabiasfactcheck.com), an independent fact-checking organization that rates news outlets on the basis of the reliability and of the political bias of the contents they produce and share. The labeling provided by MBFC, retrieved in June 2019, ranges from Extreme Left to Extreme Right for political bias. The total number of media outlets for which we have a political label is 2,190.

span.label: two of the Facebook datasets are labelled binary - provaccines/antivaccines, proscience/conspiracy - by the page a post appeared on, not by the content itself
span.quote: For the two datasets Science and Conspiracy and Vaccines, data were labeled in a binary way, respectively, provaccines/antivaccines and proscience/conspiracy, based on the page where they were posted.

span.label: interaction networks are reconstructed differently on each platform, and where direct relations are unavailable a proxy is assumed - a link between two users who commented on the same post
span.quote: In some cases, direct relations between users are not available in the data, so one needs to assume some proxy for social connections, for example, a link between two users if they comment on the same post on Facebook.

span.label: the differences across platforms could be an artefact of the different topics sampled, which is why one common topic had to be compared separately
span.quote: The striking differences observed across social media, in terms of homophily in the interaction networks and information diffusion, could be attributed to the different topics taken into account. For this reason, here we compare Facebook and Reddit on a common topic, news consumption.

span.label: the susceptible-infected-recovered epidemic model, carried from epidemiology to measure which users a message reaches and with what leaning
span.quote: These results indicate that information diffusion is biased toward individuals who share a similar leaning in some social media, namely Twitter and Facebook. In contrast, in others—Reddit and Gab in our analysis—this effect is absent.

span.label: homophily and community detection, carried from network science into a test of a psychological construct
span.quote: Then, we use these elements to assess echo chambers’ presence by looking at two different aspects: 1) homophily in interactions concerning a specific topic and 2) bias in information diffusion from like-minded sources.

span.label: comparing Facebook and Reddit on one common topic - news consumption - because the cross-platform differences could otherwise be attributed to the different topics
span.note: eliminates: a cross-platform difference that is a difference of topic, since the platforms are compared on one common topic · outcome: held
span.quote: The striking differences observed across social media, in terms of homophily in the interaction networks and information diffusion, could be attributed to the different topics taken into account. For this reason, here we compare Facebook and Reddit on a common topic, news consumption.

span.label: requiring polarization and homophilic interaction to be quantified independently, so that neither is evidence for the other
span.note: eliminates: polarization and homophily each being taken as evidence for the other, which would make an echo chamber unfalsifiable · outcome: held
span.quote: Crucially, the two elements characterizing the presence of echo chambers, polarization and homophilic interactions, should be quantified independently.

span.label: three separate measures applied to the same comparison - neighbour-leaning correlation, community structure, and SIR influence sets
span.note: eliminates: an echo-chamber result that exists only under one operationalisation of clustering · outcome: held
span.quote: One can see that all three measures confirm the picture obtained for other datasets: On Facebook, we observe a clear separation among users depending on their leaning, while, on Reddit, users’ leanings are more homogeneous and show only one peak.

span.label: choosing two platforms that already share a leaning definition and a network rationale, so the cross-comparison is not itself a methodological artefact
span.note: eliminates: that a difference between Facebook and Reddit is a difference in how leaning was defined or how connections were counted, rather than in the platforms
span.quote: Facebook and Reddit are particularly apt to a cross-comparison since they share the definition of individual leaning (computed by using the classification provided by mediabiasfactcheck.org; see Materials and Methods for further details) and the rationale in creating connections among users that is based on an interaction network.

span.label: echo chambers
span.quote: We can broadly define echo chambers as environments in which the opinion, political leaning, or belief of users about a topic gets reinforced due to repeated interactions with peers or sources having similar tendencies and attitudes.

span.label: observables
span.quote: We introduce an operational definition of echo chambers to provide a common methodological ground to explore how different platforms influence their formation. In particular, we operationalize the two common elements that characterize echo chambers into observables that can be quantified and empirically measured, namely, 1) the inference of the user’s leaning for a specific topic (e.g., politics, vaccines) and 2) the structure of their social interactions on the platform.

span.label: operational definition
span.quote: We introduce an operational definition of echo chambers to provide a common methodological ground to explore how different platforms influence their formation. In particular, we operationalize the two common elements that characterize echo chambers into observables that can be quantified and empirically measured, namely, 1) the inference of the user’s leaning for a specific topic (e.g., politics, vaccines) and 2) the structure of their social interactions on the platform.

span.label: homophily
span.quote: Then, we use these elements to assess echo chambers’ presence by looking at two different aspects: 1) homophily in interactions concerning a specific topic and 2) bias in information diffusion from like-minded sources.

span.label: polarization
span.quote: Note that polarization can happen independently from the structure or the very presence of social interactions.

span.label: group polarization
span.quote: According to group polarization theory, an echo chamber can act as a mechanism to reinforce an existing opinion within a group and, as a result, move the entire group toward more extreme positions.

span.label: Selective exposure
span.quote: Selective exposure and confirmation bias (i.e., the tendency to seek information adhering to preexisting opinions) may explain the emergence of echo chambers on social media.

span.quote: Furthermore, we find significant differences across platforms in terms of homophilic patterns in the network structure and biases in the information diffusion toward like-minded users. A clear-cut distinction emerges between social media having a feed algorithm tweakable by the users (e.g., Reddit) and social media that don’t provide such an option (e.g., Facebook and Twitter).

span.quote: Furthermore, we find significant differences across platforms in terms of homophilic patterns in the network structure and biases in the information diffusion toward like-minded users. A clear-cut distinction emerges between social media having a feed algorithm tweakable by the users (e.g., Reddit) and social media that don’t provide such an option (e.g., Facebook and Twitter).

span.label: Gab
span.quote: Gab claims to be a social platform aimed at protecting freedom of speech. However, low moderation and regulation on content has resulted in widespread hate speech. For these reasons, it has been repeatedly suspended by its service provider, and its mobile app has been banned from both App and Play stores.

span.label: feed algorithm

A clear-cut distinction emerges between social media having a feed algorithm tweakable by the users (e.g., Reddit) and social media that don’t provide such an option (e.g., Facebook and Twitter).

span.label: Media Bias/Fact Check
span.quote: The labeling of news outlets is based on the information reported by Media Bias/Fact Check (MBFC) (https://mediabiasfactcheck.com), an independent fact-checking organization that rates news outlets on the basis of the reliability and of the political bias of the contents they produce and share. The labeling provided by MBFC, retrieved in June 2019, ranges from Extreme Left to Extreme Right for political bias. The total number of media outlets for which we have a political label is 2,190.

span.label: echo chamber effect - ON FACEBOOK AND TWITTER: strong correlation between a user's leaning and their neighbourhood's, communities spanning the spectrum but internally homogeneous, and diffusion biased toward like-minded peers
span.quote: These results indicate that information diffusion is biased toward individuals who share a similar leaning in some social media, namely Twitter and Facebook. In contrast, in others—Reddit and Gab in our analysis—this effect is absent.

span.label: echo chamber effect - ON REDDIT AND GAB: absent. Users form a single community rather than opposed clusters, and the leaning of the influence set does not depend on the leaning of the seed
span.quote: The corresponding plots in Fig. 1 display a single bright area, indicating that users do not split into groups with opposite leaning but form a single community, biased to the left (Reddit) or the right (Gab).

span.label: that absence - READING 1: the platform is not producing echo chambers, which is what the measurement appears to say
span.quote: Such a latter configuration may depend upon two factors: 1) Gab and Reddit are not bursting the echo chamber effects, or 2) we are observing the dynamic inside a single echo chamber.

span.label: that absence - READING 2: the whole platform IS a single echo chamber, so there is no contrast left inside the data to detect. The authors name both and do not choose
span.quote: Such a latter configuration may depend upon two factors: 1) Gab and Reddit are not bursting the echo chamber effects, or 2) we are observing the dynamic inside a single echo chamber.

span.label: qualifies → single-platform findings about echo chambers, which cannot distinguish a property of online interaction from a property of one platform's design
span.quote: Furthermore, we find significant differences across platforms in terms of homophilic patterns in the network structure and biases in the information diffusion toward like-minded users. A clear-cut distinction emerges between social media having a feed algorithm tweakable by the users (e.g., Reddit) and social media that don’t provide such an option (e.g., Facebook and Twitter).

span.label: builds-on → group polarization theory and the selective-exposure account of why echo chambers form
span.quote: According to group polarization theory, an echo chamber can act as a mechanism to reinforce an existing opinion within a group and, as a result, move the entire group toward more extreme positions.

span.label: reconciles → the dispute over whether echo chambers exist at all - by showing the answer differs by platform under one measurement
span.quote: Echo chambers have been shown to exist in various forms of online media such as blogs, forums, and social media sites. Some studies point out echo chambers as an emerging effect of human tendencies, such as selective exposure, contagion, and group polarization. However, recently, the effects and the very existence of echo chambers have been questioned. This issue is also fueled by the scarcity of comparative studies on social media, especially concerning news consumption.

span.label: the susceptible-infected-recovered epidemic model, in which each agent is unaware, aware and willing to spread, or knowledgeable but no longer transmitting
span.quote: Classical epidemic models such as the susceptible–infected–recovered (SIR) model have been used to study the diffusion of information, such as rumors or news. In the SIR model, each agent can be in any of three states: susceptible (unaware of the circulating information), infectious (aware and willing to spread it further), or recovered (knowledgeable but not ready to transmit it anymore).
